frozen: 2026-11-01, before any sailing quantity is extracted from CLIWOC. Known: T6 (Casson) and T7 (ORBIS July edges) with the current constants and with the first sailing addendum's variants (output/polity_sail_20261101/sail.json).
why: The sailing constants that shape speed (the light-wind factor: full speed from FULL_WIND = 6 m/s, at least LIGHT_AIRS = 0.25 of it; the close-hauled share 0.85) were set from Casson's prose; the first addendum showed Casson and ORBIS cannot choose between them without a third, independent record. CLIWOC's logbooks give sailing ships' daily runs with the wind they logged.
data: CLIWOC 2.1 (Garcia-Herrera et al. 2005; historicalclimatology.com, CC BY 3.0), IMMA fields: YR MO DY, LAT LON, ID (ship), D (wind direction, degrees from which it blows; 361 calm, 362 variable), W (wind speed, m/s from the logged Beaufort terms)
extraction: consecutive days of one ship (same ID, dates one day apart), both with a position and a wind (D 1-360, W > 0); run = great-circle distance between the two positions (km per day), course = the bearing between them; theta = the angle between the course and the downwind direction (D + 180) on the first day; runs over 450 km or under 5 km a day dropped (errors, at anchor)
derivation: relative run r = run / the median run with theta <= 60 deg and W >= 10 m/s. FULL_WIND and LIGHT_AIRS: least squares of g(W) = clip(W / FULL_WIND, LIGHT_AIRS, 1) on the medians of r in 1 m/s bins of W (theta <= 90 deg). CLOSE_HAULED_SHARE: the median r with theta in [95, 115] deg and W >= FULL_WIND. SAIL_FAIR_KNOTS stays 5 (Casson; CLIWOC's ships are larger and faster, so only the shape is taken from them).
tests: T6 (Casson, Spearman and median |log(model / Casson)|) and T7 (ORBIS July coastal and overseas edges, Spearman and median |log(model / ORBIS)|), the CLIWOC constants against today's, scripts/polity_sail_check.py's definitions
adopt_if: T7 Spearman not lower by more than 0.01, T7 median |log| lower, and T6 median |log| not higher. Then polity.transport takes the constants and the three atlases' political reach is rebuilt.
